s: Cross-platform mobile and web push notification delivery via APNs, FCM, and web push protocols.
w: Receives notification requests (device tokens, title, body, data payload) via API, routes to the appropriate platform protocol (Apple Push Notification Service for iOS, Firebase Cloud Messaging for Android, Web Push for browsers), handles token management (invalid tokens purged), delivery tracking, and rich notification rendering (images, action buttons, silent/background pushes for data sync).
use: Mobile app notifications: new messages, order updates, social interactions
Web browser notifications for real-time updates (chat, news, collaboration)
Background data sync triggering app content refresh
Time-sensitive alerts requiring immediate user attention on mobile
avoid: Non-urgent notifications where email is more appropriate and less intrusive
Communication requiring rich formatting or long-form content (use in-app or email)
Users who have disabled push permissions (handle gracefully with fallback channels)
pits: Stale device tokens causing silent failures - implement token refresh and invalidation handling
Over-notification causing users to disable push entirely - respect frequency caps and preferences
tips: Platform-specific limits: APNs has connection limits, FCM has message queue limits per device
Silent/background pushes are powerful for data sync but have strict payload size limits (4KB)
